title: Modules courbes elliptiques en caractéristiques ≠2 : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: Grothendieck is redoing the transcendental description of elliptic curves over C, as preparation for moduli of elliptic curves (char ≠ 2). From the previous page, a complex elliptic curve E is described by three data. (a) Π = π_1(E,0) ≅ Z², a lattice. (b) An orientation ω of V = Π⊗R, equivalently a generator of Λ²Π. (c) A non-real complex line L ⊂ V_C = Π⊗C lying in the connected component Σ*_{V,ω} of Σ_V∖Σ_{V,R} that corresponds to ω. Here Σ_V = P(V_C) ≅ P¹(C), Σ_{V,R} = P(V) ≅ P¹(R), and the non-real points of Σ_V correspond to complex structures on V.

On this page a 'Torelli rigidification' is defined: an isomorphism u: Z² → Π (eq. 18) compatible with orientations. That means z_1∧z_2 = ω, where z_i = u(e_i) (eq. 19); in modern terms, an oriented marking of H_1(E,Z), i.e. a reduction of the structure group to SL(2,Z). Tensoring with R gives R² ≅ V (eq. 20), hence P¹_R ≅ P¹(V), P¹(C) ≅ Σ_V and D ≅ Σ*_{V,ω} (eq. 21). D is the Poincaré upper half-plane {Im z > 0} (eq. 22). The model Σ*_{R²,ω_0} is identified with D by sending z to the line L_z = C·(z,1) = C(z e_1 + e_2) (eq. 23).

Conclusion: isomorphism classes of elliptic curves with Torelli rigidification are in bijection with the points of D. SL(2,Z) acts on the right by precomposing the marking (18) with automorphisms of Z². The forgetful quotient therefore gives D/SL(2,Z), the classical analytic moduli space.

A margin note records a convention check. With the base (e_1,e_2) and the line C(1,z) instead of C(z,1), the component Σ*_{R²,ω_0} corresponds to D⁻ rather than D⁺.

The next page makes the dictionary explicit. Through φ: L_z → V, λ ↦ Re(λ(z e_1 + e_2)), the induced complex structure on R² gives e_2/e_1 = −z̄. So the parameter attached to a marking (z_1,z_2) is z = −conj(z_2/z_1), not the naive period ratio. Grothendieck is carefully tracking the sign and conjugation conventions that make the period map land in D, and that make the SL(2,Z) action come out as the standard fractional linear action.
errors: No mathematical error on this page itself; everything is convention-setting.

The margin remark (C(1,z) gives D⁻) and the next page's computation show the orientation/conjugation conventions are delicate. With L_z = C(z,1) used as the identification L ≅ V via real parts, the period ratio is z_2/z_1 = −z̄ rather than z.

The next page's line '(−x+iy)^- = −x−iy = −z … ∈ D⁻' contains a slip in bookkeeping: −x+iy itself already lies in D, and −x−iy equals −z only when x = 0, so the step does not hold as written. The final formula z = −conj(z_2/z_1) is consistent. This is not an error on the present page.

ideas.what: Elliptic curve over C described as a lattice Π, an orientation ω, and a non-real complex line L ⊂ Π⊗C in the component determined by ω
ideas.modern_name: Hodge-theoretic / period description of complex tori (weight-one Hodge structure of rank 2 with polarization given by orientation)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Weierstrass, Riemann; Hodge structures by Deligne)

ideas.what: Torelli rigidification: oriented isomorphism Z² ≅ H_1(E,Z), whose classes are parametrized by the upper half-plane
ideas.modern_name: Marked elliptic curves / Teichmüller space of genus 1 = upper half-plane; period map
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Teichmüller theory for genus 1; standard in Deligne–Rapoport, Mumford era)

ideas.what: Right action of SL(2,Z) on markings, giving D/SL(2,Z) as moduli
ideas.modern_name: Modular group action on the upper half-plane; analytic moduli stack [D/SL(2,Z)]

deep.surprise_reason: Standard textbook material (marked elliptic curves ↔ upper half-plane). The only distinctive feature is Grothendieck's careful, coordinate-free treatment of orientation and conjugation conventions, which is pedagogical rather than new.
transcription_corrections: Target of (18) is the lattice Π (handwritten Π, not H): '(18) Z² → Π'. Likewise later read 'L ⊂ Π ⊗_Z C' and 'Z² ≃ Π'.
In (21) the third isomorphism is D ≃ Σ*_{V,ω}.
'identifié à Σ*_{R²,ω_0} en identifiant z ∈ D à la droite (23) L_z = C·(z,1)', with the annotation 'z e_1 + e_2' under (z,1).
Margin note at right: 'Ainsi, les classes d'isomorphie de courbes elliptiques avec rigidification de Torelli sont en bijection avec les points de D.'
Left margin note: 'Si (e_1,e_2) base canonique de R² : en associant à z ∈ C la droite C(1,z), alors Σ*_{R²,ω_0} correspond au demi-plan D⁻ ; D = D⁺'.

Last lines read approximately: 'Dans l'ensemble des classes d'isomorphie de courbes elliptiques E = (Π, ω, L ⊂ Π⊗_Z C), avec rigidification de Torelli Z² ≃ Π, le groupe SL(2,Z) opère à droite de façon évidente, par composition à droite de (18) avec les automorphismes de Z².'
